claims.text: Introducing controlled lattice distortion through alloying can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in an eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Boron or carbon alloying can induce lattice distortion in an eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The alloying-induced lattice distortion results in increased dislocation density.
Lattice distortion increases strength by creating additional obstacles to dislocation motion.
A controlled amount of lattice distortion enhances ductility by promoting dislocation glide and cross-slip.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the as-cast alloy without the alloying addition.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by 30% relative to the as-cast alloy without the alloying addition.
The simultaneous improvement is expected when processing preserves the eutectic microstructure.
The simultaneous improvement is expected only within a specific range of lattice distortion.
